anomalies.observed: C13 is labelled "0.1mF 50V". That is 100 µF, not 0.1 µF. It sits in the same region as the 0.1 µF / 50 V decoupling capacitors nearby (C12, C14, C26, C31), and its value is not consistent with a 50 V decoupling part of this size.
anomalies.expected: A 0.1 µF ("0.1uF 50V") decoupling capacitor, matching the rest of the 50 V 0.1 µF decoupling on this board. The specification does not give a value for C13, so this is judged from its role and from the other decoupling capacitors.

evidence.quote: C13 0.1mF 50V 10K R28 (CM4 motherboard sheet, page 1, mid-left of the I/O region near JP12/JP14)
Where the spec is silent, judge the design with standard electrical-engineering practice and with the component's own metadata.

anomalies.impact: A 100 µF capacitor in a decoupling position is physically and electrically mismatched. It could cause a footprint or fit problem, and it would not give the intended high-frequency decoupling.

anomalies.observed: The schematic text carries two different values for R48. One listing gives "10K R48" and another gives "R48 210K". Both are on the Q9 AO3401A load network.
anomalies.expected: A single consistent value for R48, which should match the pull-up value used elsewhere for the switch and load networks (10K).
anomalies.impact: If R48 is 210K instead of 10K, the gate pull-up of the P-channel switch Q9 would be far weaker, which could slow switching or leave the load state uncertain.
